Okeanis (ECO) is down 7.2% today mostly because it went ex-dividend. It is not a news-driven selloff.

**The ex-dividend date explains the drop.** The company declared a $7.00 per share dividend for Q3. The NYSE ex-dividend date is today, Nov 23, and payment is Dec 1. Oslo went ex on Nov 20. At about 85 before the open, $7.00 is roughly 8%. The 7.2% drop (1.3 ATR) is therefore at or below the dividend. The "down 11.2% over 20 sessions" figure is also inflated by the dividend. The 50-day and 20-day levels in the screen are not dividend-adjusted. I did not confirm the prior close, and I found no ECO-specific news today.

**The story:**
- **Q3 was the best quarter in the company's history.** EPS was $7.67 and profit $299.6M. Fleetwide time-charter-equivalent (TCE, daily earnings per ship) was $206,800/day, with VLCCs (very large crude carriers) at $269,300/day.
- **Q4 is already largely booked at high rates.** VLCCs have 48% of spot days booked at $688,800/day and 87% of all operating days at $430,300/day. Suezmaxes have 60% booked at $410,900/day. Earnings for the next two quarters are mostly locked in.
- **The balance sheet is stronger.** Quarter-end cash was $233.1M. One secondary source puts debt at $704M and market-adjusted net loan-to-value below 20%. The company's own release gave no debt figure.
- **The cash question.** One outside analysis says the dividend needs about $273M against $233M of cash, which would mean relying on Q4 collections. That is an outside estimate and not company guidance.

**The risk is spot rates.**
- Gulf-to-China VLCC rates fell about 64% from the Oct 8 record to Nov 13 (841 to about 308 Worldscale).
- Causes were Gulf exports returning to near pre-war levels, fewer long-haul cargoes, more ballasting ships East of Suez, and less war premium on hopes of Iran talks. Oil is down about 20% this month.
- An Arrow Shipbroking analyst called the drop "exaggerated". Kpler expects more near-term pressure on Gulf-to-China, but a rebound on US Gulf-to-China.
- Sanctions relief on the shadow fleet (tankers moving sanctioned oil) is another reported risk to rates.
- Longer term, orders equal about 32% of the VLCC fleet for 2028-29 delivery.

**What could move it over the next 1-10 sessions:**
- **Iran or Hormuz headlines.** A deal or de-escalation hurts rates and the stock. Renewed attacks help them.
- **Weekly VLCC rate prints (Baltic Exchange).** A bounce would help. Further falls would hurt.
- **Oil price direction.**
- **Peer moves** from Frontline, DHT and International Seaways.
- **The Dec 1 dividend payment.** Any sign of a cash squeeze would be a negative.
- **No earnings catalyst.** The next report is 2027-02-17.

**Read for the journal:** Today's drop is mechanical, not a signal of new weakness or a fresh dip to buy. After adjusting for the dividend, the stock is roughly flat to slightly down on the day, and its trend has been rolling over since the October peak (about 99 on Oct 14, 82.21 on Nov 9). Rate momentum is negative, but Q4 earnings are mostly locked in, which limits fundamental downside in the short run. The next few sessions depend on Iran and oil headlines, not on anything specific to Okeanis. I would not treat the 7.2% drop as a mean-reversion setup.

**Gaps:**
- I could not read the call transcript, so management's remarks are secondhand.
- I found no post-Q3 analyst targets.
- Search found no news dated Nov 17-23 on Iran, oil or tanker rates, so the latest rate data is from Nov 13-16.

**Ashland (ASH): research at 12:15 PM CT, Monday 2026-11-23**

I found no news that explains today's 3.6% drop. The story is a stock held up by takeover hopes, weighed down by a soft quarter, and now selling off on a day the market rallied.

**Business**
- Ashland makes specialty chemicals for personal care, pharma and coatings.
- FY26 sales were $1.863B and adjusted EBITDA was $385M. That was at the low end of a trimmed guidance range.
- The Q4 report on Nov 3 missed on adjusted EPS: $1.12 against about $1.27 to $1.30 expected.
- Specialty Additives EBITDA fell 31% to $20M. The causes were weak energy-market demand and poor productivity at the Hopewell plant, which makes hydroxyethylcellulose (HEC), a thickener.
- Life Sciences set a record 35.6% EBITDA margin.
- The GAAP loss was $17M for the quarter.
- FY27 guidance is EBITDA of $405M to $435M and sales of $1.905B to $1.975B. A review of the quarter (Earnings Whispers) called that roughly in line with expectations, not ahead of them.
- The guidance depends on Hopewell output rising about 25%. Management said "the Hopewell drag is finished now," but about $5M of under-absorption is expected to carry into Q1.
- Balance sheet: net leverage is 2.3x, liquidity is $976M, and there were no buybacks in FY26.

**Takeover angle (the main driver of the stock)**
- Activist Ancora pushed for a sale in June. Its base case was about $76 a share, and its bull case was about $96.
- Ashland settled with Ancora in late July, adding two directors and a capital-allocation committee. Cruiser Capital also pushed for a sale.
- Bloomberg reported in August that Ashland was weighing a sale after interest from Advent, Apollo and Carlyle. Citi and Lazard are advising. Standard Investments holds 9.89%.
- Ashland collected initial bids around Oct 2. Mergermarket named a CD&R and Clariant consortium, with Apollo, Carlyle and possibly CVC also circling.
- Mergermarket said even a 10% to 15% premium may be hard for some sponsors to finance.
- Reuters reported on Oct 22 that Evonik is weighing a bid. Ashland's market value was put at about $3.3B.
- The Earnings Whispers page says Bloomberg reported on Nov 22 that Clariant and CD&R are in talks to buy Ashland. I could not find the Bloomberg article itself, so treat that as unverified.
- No offer has been announced. On the Q4 call, questions about a sale went unanswered.

**What could move it in the next 1 to 10 sessions**
- **Up:** A confirmed deal or a named bidder, or a report that talks are advancing, would likely lift the stock. Ancora's base-case value of about $76 is roughly 9% above 69.77.
- **Down:** Reports that the process has stalled, or that sponsors can't make the numbers work, would hurt. The stock has no earnings catalyst until 2027-02-01, and the Q4 miss means little support without a deal.
- **Unknown:** I found no news on why it fell today while SPY rose. A fade in deal premium is plausible but unconfirmed.
- Takeover-speculation names can gap sharply either way, and a deal announcement could come at any time.

- **Nov 17 drop:** CRM fell 9.5% to $194.52 with no company announcement, filing or earnings. Trefis says 57 of 62 comparable software names fell too, but CRM fell more than three times the group median of 3.0%. The trigger was a string of tech outages that raised worries about AI misuse hitting software. Newsweek says it fell about 10.7% for the week by Wednesday. CRM is hit harder than peers because its strategy rests on AI agents running inside its software.
- **Company-specific pressure:**
  - S&P cut Salesforce's credit rating from A+ to A on Nov 4, citing acquisitions and the $25B debt-funded buyback.
  - It agreed on Oct 20 to buy Braze for about $5.66B in cash, with closing expected in fiscal 2028.
  - Business Insider reported new layoffs this week; Salesforce hasn't confirmed the size.
  - Newsweek also mentions third-party attacks tied to its platform (Optimizely, Gainsight).
- **Fundamentals haven't broken (Q2 FY27, reported Aug 26):**
  - Revenue was $11.3B, up 11%, and cRPO (contracted revenue not yet recognized) was $33.5B, up 14% in constant currency.
  - Agentforce (its AI-agent product) ARR passed $1.5B, up more than 240%.
  - Free cash flow rose 81%, and full-year revenue guidance was raised to $46.1B–$46.4B.
  - Weak spots: only 11–12% growth, and the acquisitions flatter the reported numbers.
- **Analysts are split.** Morgan Stanley downgraded in July with a $185 target, and KeyBanc downgraded on weak Agentforce evidence. A search snippet says BofA upgraded to Buy with a $285 target, but I couldn't confirm the date, so don't lean on it. The stock sits near the $185 targets of the bears.

**What could move it over the next few sessions**
- **Earnings on Dec 2 after the close** (call at 2:00 PM PT / 4:00 PM CT), which is session 7.
  - Q3 guidance is revenue of $11.42B–$11.5B, non-GAAP EPS of $3.42–$3.44 and cRPO growth of about 14%.
  - The cRPO number and Agentforce ARR are what the market will judge.
  - I found no current options-implied move. Past quarters implied roughly 5–9%.
- **Run-up:** a depressed stock ahead of a print can squeeze higher if software keeps rebounding. A hold above the 20-day low of $179.92 supports that.
- **More AI-scare headlines or a new model launch.** These have hit software repeatedly this year (April 8 and Nov 17).
- **Deal and layoff news:** layoff confirmation, any Braze regulatory news, and another leveraged deal would all matter.
- **Analyst moves** before earnings, in either direction.

**Caveats**
- I found no news coverage of today's move or of Nov 19–21. I can't verify SPY up 4.7%, which is extreme. If it's real, today's CRM bounce is mostly market beta, and CRM lagging a very strong tape on light volume (0.6 times normal) is a weak sign.

  - Treasury Secretary Bessent called for an outsider to replace Huang.

  - The Nasdaq fell about 10%, its worst week since March 2020, and the S&P 500 fell about 8.6% to 6,910.39.

- Nomura's McElligott said much of the move is "a massive surge of MECHANICAL buying" from short covering and options hedging. He said not to read it as an all-clear.
- Capital Economics (via CNN's headline, which I couldn't open) also called it largely mechanical.

- Ed Yardeni sees no bear market but cut his year-end S&P target to 7,500.

  - A reported SEC probe over the Huang revelations.

  - Any reversal of the reinstatement.
- **AI sentiment:** Anthropic trades near $88, just above its IPO price. Its pending debt rating is expected to be high-yield. Capex-cut estimates could return. Remaining earnings this week are small: HPE, Agilent and Zoom.

**Net:** this is a headline-driven, squeeze-assisted rebound after a washout, with the catalyst (Huang) still legally and politically unsettled. The macro backdrop is a likely Fed hike, high yields and an oil shock, so follow-through is uncertain and a partial give-back is plausible.

- The stock was already down about 24% from its prior report before this one. Bullish sentiment had dropped from 46% to 19%.

- One source (AAII) shows one analyst downgrade and no upgrades in the month to Nov 12. It doesn't name the firm. A headline says Oppenheimer cut its target to $210 after the print.
- The stock is cheap at roughly 12.5 times earnings, but that rests on 45X-boosted earnings.

**What is driving the stock now: a possible takeover with no premium.** On Sunday 11-22, Bloomberg reported that Clariant (a Swiss specialty chemicals company) and CD&R (a private equity firm) are in talks to buy Ashland. The deal would be all cash, at a value "close to Friday's share price", about $3.39B (roughly $3.3B by another count). No per-share price was published.
- A deal "could come together within days", but talks could collapse or another bidder could appear. Ashland and Clariant declined to comment, and CD&R did not respond.
- The stock is down 3.6% today on a day SPY is up 4.7%. The likely reason is that the report points to roughly no premium. That is my inference. I found no article that explains today's drop.
- Ashland's own price history shows the stock ran from about $68.76 in early October to a $77.70 close on 11-9, on sale hopes. Friday's close was 72.40, and today it is about 69.8. The earlier run-up on sale hopes is now fading.
- Ancora's base-case sale value was $76.47 a share (11.5x EBITDA), and its bull case was about $96. A near-market price falls well short of both.

**How the sale process got here**
- Ancora (activist) pushed for a sale in June. In late July it settled for two board seats and a capital-allocation committee, not a sale process. Cruiser Capital (another activist, owning 0.15%) also pressed for a sale and threatened a proxy fight.
- Bloomberg reported in August that Ashland was exploring a sale, with Citigroup and Lazard advising. Apollo, Carlyle, Advent and Standard Industries (a roughly 9.9% holder) were named as interested. The stock rose 6% on that news.
- Ashland collected initial bids on 10-2. CD&R and Clariant were reported as a consortium. Clariant would face antitrust overlap in personal care if it bid alone.
- On the 11-3 call, management did not answer questions about a sale process.

**Fundamentals (fiscal Q4 report, 11-3)**
- Adjusted EPS was $1.12, against a $1.27–$1.30 consensus. That is a miss. Sales were $498M (+4%). The GAAP result was a $17M loss from continuing operations, driven by impairments, restructuring and the Argentine entity.
- Adjusted EBITDA was $121M (+2%) and has risen each quarter this year ($98M, $109M, $121M).
- Life Sciences had a record 35.6% margin. Personal Care grew 8%. Specialty Additives EBITDA fell 31% on the weak Hopewell plant and soft energy demand.
- The fiscal 2027 outlook is sales of $1.905–1.975B and adjusted EBITDA of $405–435M, up from $385M. Reviewers called it roughly in line, and it depends on Hopewell recovering (about 25% more output).
- Net debt is $891M (2.3x leverage), with $976M of liquidity.
- The stock rose from 73.02 to 76.44 after the report.

**What could move it over the next 1–10 sessions**

- **Deal at a visible premium, or a rival bid (Apollo, Carlyle, Advent, Standard):** a sharp jump.
